content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To make a chipmunk puppet from a glove, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Sketch the chipmunk's facial features on a template (10 minutes)
Step 2. Cut the pinkie and thumb off an old brown glove (5 minutes)
Step 3. Stitch the glove openings closed where the fingers were removed (15 minutes)
Step 4. Sort through a button jar for two black eyes (10 minutes)
Step 5. Glue the felt ears onto the top of the glove head (5 minutes)
Step 6. Cut out small circles of white felt for the eye backings (3 minutes)
Step 7. Purchase a bag of polyester fiberfill stuffing (30 minutes)
Step 8. Cut a small piece of black embroidery floss for the nose (2 minutes)
Step 9. Apply a small amount of pink blush to the puppet's cheeks (1 minute)
Step 10. Unroll a length of tan yarn for the belly patch (2 minutes)
Step 11. Sew the stuffed tail onto the back of the glove (20 minutes)
Step 12. Stuff the main body of the glove with fiberfill (10 minutes)
Step 13. Measure the length of the middle finger for the head size (2 minutes)
Step 14. Embroider the tiny chipmunk smile (15 minutes)
Step 15. Knit a tiny sweater for the puppet (2 hours)
Step 16. Cut out a long strip of faux fur for the tail (5 minutes)
Step 17. Draw the stripe pattern onto the fur strip (5 minutes)
Step 18. Find a pair of fabric scissors (2 minutes)
Step 19. Fold the fur strip in half lengthwise (2 minutes)
Step 20. Insert a wire armature into the body for posing (12 minutes)
Step 21. Thread a needle with heavy-duty brown thread (1 minute)
Step 22. Trace a small triangle for the nose onto felt (4 minutes)
Step 23. Locate the fabric glue in the craft drawer (5 minutes)
Step 24. Brush the faux fur to make it fluffy (3 minutes)
Step 25. Paint three dark stripes onto the back of the glove (20 minutes)
Step 26. Secure the thread with a double knot (1 minute)
Step 27. Clean the workspace to prepare for assembly (15 minutes)
Step 28. Set the puppet on a stand to dry (1 hour)
Step 29. Select a small bead for the nose (2 minutes)
Step 30. Wash the old glove to ensure it is clean (40 minutes)
Step 31. Stuff the head section firmly (5 minutes)
Step 32. Trim any loose threads from the glove (4 minutes)
Step 33. Sew the fur strip into a tube shape (25 minutes)
Step 34. Research chipmunk markings online for accuracy (20 minutes)
Step 35. Glue the white felt circles onto the head (5 minutes)
Step 36. Attach the black button eyes (10 minutes)
Step 37. Position the arms of the puppet (5 minutes)
Step 38. Spray the puppet with a fabric protector (5 minutes)
Step 39. Cut a cardboard disc for the base of the neck (6 minutes)
Step 40. Hand-wash the finished face area (5 minutes)
Step 41. Sharpen the fabric chalk (1 minute)
Step 42. Sew the neck disc inside the glove (15 minutes)
Step 43. Wind a bobbin with matching brown thread (3 minutes)
Step 44. Measure the tail length against the glove (2 minutes)
Step 45. Heat up the hot glue gun (8 minutes)
Step 46. Apply glue to the back of the buttons (2 minutes)
Step 47. Braid three strands of yarn for a decorative scarf (15 minutes)
Step 48. Trim the excess wire from the armature (4 minutes)
Step 49. Cut the tail shape out of the faux fur (7 minutes)
Step 50. Photograph the progress of the puppet (5 minutes)
Step 51. Sew the tiny sweater onto the puppet body (30 minutes)
Step 52. Stuff the arms of the glove (8 minutes)
Step 53. Sign the bottom of the puppet (1 minute)
Step 54. Dress the puppet in its accessories (10 minutes)
Step 55. Iron the glove flat (6 minutes)
Step 56. Stuff the tail tube with fiberfill (10 minutes)
Step 57. Glue the black bead nose onto the face (3 minutes)
Step 58. Embroider tiny claws onto the fingertips (25 minutes)
Step 59. Cut a small piece of tan felt for the belly (4 minutes)
Step 60. Buy a set of fine-tipped fabric markers (45 minutes)
Step 61. Stitch the tan felt belly onto the glove (20 minutes)
Step 62. Prepare a bowl of warm soapy water (5 minutes)
Step 63. Turn the glove inside out (2 minutes)
Step 64. Turn the glove right side out again (2 minutes)
Step 65. Inspect the puppet for any holes (5 minutes)
Step 66. Allow the fabric glue to cure (4 hours)
Step 67. Gather all necessary sewing supplies (10 minutes)
Step 68. Apply a clear coat to the bead nose (10 minutes)
Step 69. Steam the puppet to remove wrinkles (12 minutes)
Step 70. Cut out two small ear shapes from brown felt (5 minutes)
